debrief_steps: Ask Apex compliance for written wording on Frankfurt tenant pinning including backups, so Petra can hand it to her legal team. (owner Jonas Weber, due 2026-10-05). Why: Jonas's compliance promise was undated and not logged. Legal wants it in writing, and it is easy to miss next to the pilot plan.

Ask Petra to confirm with Milan whether Apex would replace the historian license renewing in March, and offer to send what finance needs to review an exception. (owner Claire Dumont, due 2026-10-06). Why: Petra and Milan disagree on whether anything gets replaced. That decides whether the freeze has an exception, and it is easy to take one side.

Ask Petra who signs and whether the CFO approves, and offer a one-page pilot summary she can bring to finance. (owner Claire Dumont, due 2026-10-07). Why: The CFO came up in passing and the CRM economic buyer is blank. Easy to treat the freeze as only a timing issue.
opponent_steps: Get written EU data-residency confirmation from compliance** - **Action:** Ask Apex compliance to confirm in writing that the tenant is pinned to Frankfurt, backups included, and to supply the contract wording. Send it to Petra for her legal team. - **Owner:** Jonas Weber starts the request with compliance. Claire Dumont owns the delivery to Petra. - **Timing:** Request it by Friday, Oct 2. Have the written answer to Petra before the Oct 5 pilot plan, and in any case before line 3 data flows on or after Oct 9. - **Why it matters:** Legal has stated a hard rule, and Jonas only gave a verbal answer. This could kill the deal, and the pilot would send plant data into the platform.

Work the budget freeze: find the economic buyer and test the historian-replacement exception** - **Action:** - Ask Petra for an intro to finance or the CFO, and learn the exception process and decision steps. - Collect the historian license cost, scope and March renewal and notice terms, and map what Apex would replace. - Update the CRM: add the economic buyer (currently blank), record the decision process (currently "not discussed"), and move the Dec 18 close date to a realistic post-April date. - **Owner:** Claire Dumont, with Milan for the historian details. - **Timing:** Send the ask to Petra in the recap email by Oct 2. Aim to have the finance conversation and the historian facts before the pilot ends. Fix the CRM this week. - **Why it matters:** The freeze, the unnamed economic buyer and the March renewal mean the Dec 18 close and the $390K forecast are unsupported. The historian renewal is the only identified path to an exception.

Send the pilot plan by Oct 5, with success criteria tied to the business case** - **Action:** - Deliver the plan with measurable criteria: downtime by cause per shift for plant managers, and quality-model hit rate on line 3. - Include data residency, the Milan controller-access dependency (due Oct 9), and the historian functions that would need to be replaced. - **Owner:** Jonas Weber, with Claire reviewing. - **Timing:** Monday, Oct 5, as committed on the call. - **Why it matters:** The pilot is the one agreed next step and keeps momentum through the freeze. Success criteria that cover the replacement case give Petra the evidence she needs for finance.

verdicts.why: A is concise and grounded: it gets legal-ready Frankfurt wording, tests the historian exception, and names the economic buyer, respecting the freeze. B adds hygiene, assumes costs and scope, and pushes finance intros and CRM changes.

A's top step is the EU residency written confirmation, the legal blocker, with timing before the pilot data flows. A also gives a fuller budget-freeze path, though it leans on CRM hygiene. B's disagreement reading is inaccurate.
